title: Longest Common Subsequence
prompt: Given two strings `text1` and `text2`, return the length of their longest common subsequence. A common subsequence is a sequence of characters that appears in both strings in the same relative order, but not necessarily contiguously. If there is no common subsequence, return 0.

examples.explanation: The longest common subsequence is "ace", with length 3.
The entire string is the common subsequence.
There is no common subsequence at all.

constraints: text1 and text2 consist of only lowercase English characters
hints: Think of comparing the strings character by character from the end (or start): if the last characters match, they must both be part of the LCS.
Define dp[i][j] as the LCS length of text1[0:i] and text2[0:j]. If text1[i-1] == text2[j-1], dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1. Otherwise dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
Build a (len(text1)+1) x (len(text2)+1) table with the first row and column initialized to 0 (empty string has no common subsequence with anything).

solution.approach: Classic 2D DP. dp[i][j] represents the LCS length between the first i characters of text1 and the first j characters of text2. Row 0 and column 0 are 0 since an empty prefix has no common subsequence. For each cell, if the current characters (text1[i-1], text2[j-1]) match, extend the diagonal's LCS by 1. Otherwise, take the best of ignoring the current character from either string: max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). The final answer is dp[len(text1)][len(text2)].
